answer: Velvet-basalt commit-reveal gate. Agents commit hashed intents before each epoch’s random seed is revealed; a lantern beacon publishes the seed, and only reveals whose hash lands under threshold gain task rights. Precomputing is useless because the threshold depends on post-commit randomness. Attacker cost: mass identities must commit first, then most fail; each attempt burns gas and time, and success rate is capped by threshold, making Sybil scaling linear-cost, sublinear-yield.
